result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A gives a clear verdict: keep annual as the default, but make the monthly price easy to read. It explains how hidden pricing turns into refunds, chargebacks and churn at renewal, and its figures ($7.50, $65.89, 42%) are correct and shown. Answer B is solid but lets small grey text pass as long as it meets contrast rules. It also says without support that annual defaults 'usually lift revenue' and cites the FTC click-to-cancel rule, which may no longer be in force, so A is stronger. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives a clearer recommendation: keep annual as the default but show the monthly price at equal weight. It explains how the small grey text could lead to refunds, chargebacks and churn, and it lays out exact plan copy with correct figures ($7.50/mo, $65.89 saved, 42%). A is solid on disclosure and measurement, but it accepts small grey text as long as it passes contrast, never states the dollar saving, and says without support that pre-selection 'usually lifts revenue'. It also cites click-to-cancel as a live rule, which is legally shaky.
